report:
### Conclusion
Contrary to your initial view, high-quality medical evidence supports this health claim: **chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation significantly reduces surgical-site infection (SSI) compared with iodine-alcohol prior to cesarean delivery.**

### Evidence Summary
* **Landmark Trial:** A randomized controlled trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated 1,147 women undergoing C-sections. Chlorhexidine-alcohol reduced SSI rates nearly by half compared to iodine-alcohol (4.0% vs. 7.3%, relative risk 0.55).
* **Cochrane Review:** A systematic review by the Cochrane Collaboration concluded with moderate certainty that preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine gluconate (especially in alcohol-based solutions) is more effective at preventing post-cesarean SSI than iodine preparations.
* **Meta-Analytic Consensus:** Systematic reviews and network meta-analyses consistently rank alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine highest in efficacy for preventing post-cesarean wound infections when compared to povidone-iodine preparations.

While isolated studies comparing chlorhexidine-alcohol to multi-step aqueous iodine scrub-and-paint protocols show equivalent infection rates, direct trial comparisons against iodine-alcohol confirm that chlorhexidine-alcohol is superior.

### Sources
1. *New England Journal of Medicine*: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048
2. *Cochrane Library*: https://www.cochrane.org/CD007462/PREG_skin-preparation-preventing-infection-following-caesarean-section
3. *PubMed*: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/
4. *Journal of Hospital Infection (ScienceDirect)*: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282
